transcript: Last night I made my way through some really smoky air here in New York to attend mtc's production of King James at City Center. This play follows the friendship of Sean and Matt, 2 guys from Cleveland who bond over their love of basketball. In each of the 4 scenes spanning over a decade, something notable happens in the career of LeBron James. These are like anchor points of the play that coincidentally align with turning points in Sean and matt's friendship. Their dynamic is really interesting, and this piece simultaneously illustrates, critiques, and appreciates some of the aspects of male friendship. On one hand, you could say basketball is all that Sean and Matt have together, but on the other hand, it's really important to them and their friendship. I had heard great things about the play, and I expected it to be well acted, but I honestly did not expect to be moved by it per se. But theater is literally magic. I mean, the fact that a play about 2 straight men obsessed with basketball made me cry. Like, how is that not sorcery? With that, another playable for my collection.
